Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

constant adjective

continual, never letting up

also constantly, continual, continually, incessant, non-stop, a constant companion

classical

Plin. Ep. 8.17.1: assiduae tempestātēs
Mart. 11.39.2: assiduusque comes

assiduus, assidua, assiduum

adjective, declension

constant, continual; always at hand

From assideō: first of a person always there, sitting at a task (a constant companion, a farmer always on his land), then of things that never let up, storms, rain, work. Constantly: assiduē (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • perpetuus, perpetua, perpetuum — unbroken, continuous

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 296: constant (incessant), perpetuus; constantly, perpetuō; Traupman 296

    Unbroken from end to end (see permanent). Constantly: perpetuō.

  • continuus, continua, continuum — continuous, one after another

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.34.4: continuōs complūrēs diēs; Traupman 296

    Of days, nights and years, following one after another without a break: continuōs complūrēs diēs, several days running. Of place, joined on, unbroken (Lewis & Short).

  • Vāde mēcum. — a constant companion (a favourite book)

    also used · modern · Traupman 254

    Literally “go with me”. We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

  • continuē — continually

    also used · classical · Traupman 296

Examples

  • num istīc quoque immīte et turbidum caelum? hīc assiduae tempestātēs et crēbra dīluvia

    is the sky wild and stormy where you are too? Here it is constant storms and one flood after anotherPlin. Ep. 8.17.1

  • cūnārum fuerās mōtor, Charidēme, meārum et puerī custōs assiduusque comes

    you rocked my cradle, Charidemus, and were my guardian as a boy and my constant companionMart. 11.39.1–2

  • Secūtae sunt continuōs complūrēs diēs tempestātēs, quae et nostrōs in castrīs continērent et hostem ā pugnā prohibērent.

    There followed several days of storms without a break, which kept our men in camp and the enemy from fighting.Caes. BG 4.34.4

See also always, permanent, often.
